baking_powder.description: Baking powder (distinct leavening from baking soda)
baking_powder.name: Baking powder

cheese_hard_grated.description: Kačkavalj or parmesan-style, grated or sliced
cheese_hard_grated.name: Grated hard cheese

pasta.description: Dry wheat pasta, any shape incl. soup pasta
pasta.name: Pasta

ravioli_cheese.description: Store-bought cheese ravioli, fresh or dried
ravioli_cheese.name: Cheese ravioli

rice_paper_wrapper.description: Dried rice paper sheets, Asian aisle
rice_paper_wrapper.name: Rice paper wrappers

rice_white.description: White rice — plain, risotto/short-grain or sushi rice all used interchangeably here
rice_white.name: Rice

2_ingredient_oat_banana_cookies.name: 2-Ingredient Oat & Banana Cookies
2_ingredient_oat_banana_cookies.note: No flour, no butter, no added sugar beyond whatever's in the raisins — the one bakery item here you can actually eat often without it working against the 1800 kcal target.
steps: Preheat oven to 180°C, line a tray.
Mash bananas, stir in oats, cinnamon and any extras until evenly combined.
Spoon 12 mounds onto the tray, flatten slightly with a fork.
Bake 15–18 min until golden at the edges.

avocado_egg_toast_seeded.name: Seeded Toast with Avocado & Egg
avocado_egg_toast_seeded.note: A heartier version of the plain avocado toast — the egg on top makes it enough to carry you to lunch. Runny yolk works best here, but cook the eggs however you like them.
steps: Toast the seeded bread.
Mash the avocado with the lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Fry or poach the eggs in a little oil to your preference.
Spread the mashed avocado over the toast, top each slice with an egg, season again, and add chili flakes if using.

avocado_tomato_toast.name: Avocado & Tomato Toast
avocado_tomato_toast.note: Avocado prices swing a lot — worth checking before making this a regular. Good with a boiled egg on top for more protein.
steps: Toast the bread.
Mash the avocado with lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Spread over the toast, top with tomato slices, season again, add chili flakes if using.

baked_gnocchi_with_tomato_mozzarella.name: Baked Gnocchi with Tomato & Mozzarella
baked_gnocchi_with_tomato_mozzarella.note: A good one to assemble ahead — build it in the morning, keep covered in the fridge, then bake at dinner time. Reheats, and even freezes, better than the pan-fried version above.
steps: Preheat oven to 200°C. Boil the gnocchi briefly, just 1–2 min until they float — they'll finish cooking in the oven, so don't fully cook them here. Drain.
Sauté onion and garlic in oil, 5 min, add the tomato sauce, simmer 8–10 min, season.
Combine the gnocchi with the sauce in a baking dish, scatter mozzarella over the top.
Bake 15–18 min until bubbling and golden in spots.

banana_bread.name: Banana Bread
banana_bread.note: One bowl, no mixer, and by far the lightest thing in this section — a good use for bananas that are about to go off, and mild enough to work as a breakfast side too. Keeps 4 days, freezes well sliced.
steps: Preheat oven to 180°C, line a loaf pan.
Mash bananas, whisk in eggs, sugar and oil.
Fold in flour, baking soda and salt — don't overmix.
Pour into the pan, bake 50–55 min until a skewer comes out clean.

bean_cheese_quesadillas.name: Bean & Cheese Quesadillas
bean_cheese_quesadillas.note: The cheesiest dish in the plan, so a good one to pair with a lighter lunch that day. No oil needed — the tortilla toasts fine dry.
steps: Spread mashed beans over half of each tortilla, scatter cheese and pepper, fold in half.
Dry-fry in a pan, 2–3 min per side, until golden and the cheese has melted.
Cut into wedges, serve with salsa.

bean_veggie_burritos.name: Bean & Veggie Burritos
bean_veggie_burritos.note: Genuinely no real cooking involved — good for a night when even 20 minutes feels like too much. Best eaten fresh, doesn't store well rolled.
steps: Warm the beans in a pan with a pinch of cumin and paprika, 5 min (or skip and use cold).
Fill tortillas with beans, corn, slaw, salsa and a squeeze of lime.
Roll up tightly, folding in the ends.

caramelized_chickpeas_cocoa.name: Caramelized Chickpeas with Cinnamon & Cocoa
caramelized_chickpeas_cocoa.note: Needs an overnight soak before you start, so plan a day ahead — the actual hands-on time is short.
steps: Soak the dry chickpeas overnight in cold water.
Drain and boil until tender (about 50 min), then cool and pat completely dry.
Mix the powdered sugar, cinnamon, cocoa and vanilla sugar in a bag or bowl, then toss the chickpeas through until evenly coated.
Spread on a parchment-lined tray and bake at 190°C for 30–40 min, stirring occasionally, until the coating turns glossy and caramelized.
Cool completely before eating — they crisp up as they cool.

ingredients.displayQty: a few torn leaves, or dried oregano

cheese_ravioli_with_tomato_butter_sauce.name: Cheese Ravioli with Tomato-Butter Sauce
cheese_ravioli_with_tomato_butter_sauce.note: Ravioli are more delicate than regular pasta — go gently at every step. Reheats fine on the stove with a splash of water to loosen the sauce, though the filling is best within 2–3 days.
steps: Sauté onion and garlic in butter, 5 min, until soft.
Add the tomato sauce or chopped tomatoes, simmer 10 min, season with oregano or basil, salt and pepper.

Meanwhile, boil the ravioli in a wide pot of salted water per packet instructions (usually 3–5 min — they float when ready). Drain gently; they tear easily, so don't stir roughly or dump them from a height.
Fold the ravioli gently into the sauce, top with grated cheese.

chili_with_beans_corn.name: Chili with Beans & Corn
chili_with_beans_corn.note: Keeps 4 days in the fridge, freezes well. You already know this one — recipe here just for the shopping list.
steps: Sauté chopped onion, garlic and pepper in oil, 5 min.
Add paprika and cumin, stir 30 seconds, then add tomatoes, beans and corn.
Simmer uncovered 20 min, stirring occasionally, until thickened. Season with salt and chili.
Serve over rice.

classic_pancakes.name: Classic Pancakes
classic_pancakes.note: Makes about 12–15 small (7–8cm) pancakes. Serve right away with berries, nuts, syrup, honey or condensed milk.
steps: Whisk the egg with sugar and salt until dissolved, then whisk in the milk and oil.
Sift the flour and baking powder together, then stir into the wet mixture — mix just until combined so the batter stays tender.
Heat a dry, smooth non-stick pan over medium heat. Pour in batter one pancake at a time and let it spread into a small round.
Flip when bubbles appear on the surface and the top looks set but still slightly moist; cook the second side until matching.
Serve warm, straight from the pan.

creamy_mushroom_soup.name: Creamy Mushroom Soup
creamy_mushroom_soup.note: Milky and comforting — basically your creamy mushroom pasta sauce thinned into a soup, with a stock cube for extra depth. Blend partway or fully if you want it smooth instead of chunky.
steps: Sauté diced onion and garlic in butter until soft, then add sliced mushrooms and cook until they release their liquid and start to brown.
Stir in the flour and cook a minute to form a roux, then gradually whisk in the milk and crumbled stock cube.
Simmer gently, stirring often, until thickened and the mushrooms are fully tender.
Season with nutmeg, pepper and salt to taste; stir through chopped parsley just before serving.

creamy_potato_leek_soup.name: Creamy Potato-Leek Soup
creamy_potato_leek_soup.note: Yogurt does the "creamy" work here instead of actual cream — most of the fat saving in this one is that swap. Keeps 4 days.
steps: Sauté leek in oil 6 min until soft, don't brown.
Add potato and stock, simmer 20 min until potato falls apart easily.
Blend smooth with an immersion blender. Off the heat, stir in yogurt (boiling it after will split it).
Season, top with chives, serve with bread.

easy_apple_pie.name: Easy Apple Pie
easy_apple_pie.note: A basic shortcrust — just butter, flour, sugar, salt and water, no special equipment. The only trick is keeping everything cold and not overworking the dough. Keeps 3 days at room temperature covered, or refrigerate in warm weather.
steps: Make the dough: rub cold butter into the flour, sugar and salt with your fingertips until it looks like coarse breadcrumbs. Add ice water 1 tbsp at a time, mixing just until it comes together — don't overwork it.
Shape into a disc, wrap, and chill 30 min (this step matters — warm dough is hard to roll and shrinks in the oven).
Preheat oven to 190°C. Split the dough roughly in half, roll one half out on a floured surface, and line a pie or tart dish, letting the edges overhang slightly.
Toss apple slices with sugar, cinnamon, lemon juice and flour. Pile into the crust.
Roll out the second half, cover the pie (whole lid with a few vent cuts, or torn strips for a rustic look), pinch the edges together, brush with egg.
Bake 50–60 min until deep golden and the filling is visibly bubbling through the vents — tent loosely with foil if the top browns too fast before that. Cool 15 min before slicing.

easy_lemon_pie.name: Easy Lemon Pie
easy_lemon_pie.note: No mixer, no pastry-making — just crush, whisk, pour. The richest thing in this whole plan, so a genuine once-in-a-while treat rather than a weekly habit. Keeps 4 days refrigerated.
steps: Preheat oven to 160°C. Mix crushed biscuits with melted butter, press firmly into a pie dish to form a crust.
Whisk condensed milk, egg yolks, lemon juice and zest together until thick and pale.
Pour over the crust, bake 15 min until just set with a slight wobble in the center (baking it briefly makes the egg yolks safe to eat, unlike a true no-bake version).
Cool, then chill at least 3 hours before slicing.

fried_chinese_style_veg_with_rice.name: Fried Chinese-Style Veg with Rice
fried_chinese_style_veg_with_rice.note: Your existing go-to — frozen mixed veg keeps this fast. Best fresh; reheats fine for 3 days.
steps: Cook rice. Meanwhile, heat oil in a wide pan or wok, add garlic and ginger, 30 sec.
Add frozen vegetables straight from the freezer, stir-fry on high heat 6–8 min.
Add soy sauce and sugar, toss. Stir in scrambled egg if using.
Serve over rice.

lentil_salad_tomato_basil.name: Lentil Salad with Tomato & Basil
lentil_salad_tomato_basil.note: A light, barely-cooked salad — boil the lentils, then toss everything else through a garlic-chili-basil infused olive oil.
steps: Boil the lentils until just tender but still holding their shape, then drain and cool slightly.
Warm the oil gently with minced garlic, chili flakes and torn basil to infuse, then set aside.
Chop the spring onion and halve the cherry tomatoes; shave the cheese with a peeler.
Toss the lentils with the vegetables and cheese, dress with the infused oil, and season with salt to taste.

loaded_baked_potatoes.name: Loaded Baked Potatoes
loaded_baked_potatoes.note: You already know this one — this version adds a low-fat topping bar instead of butter and sour cream. For a richer night, spoon over the mushroom white sauce from Pasta with Creamy Mushroom Sauce (Italian) instead of the toppings bar. Reheats fine 3 days; keep toppings separate from the potatoes if storing.
steps: Preheat oven to 210°C. Prick potatoes, bake directly on the rack 40–45 min until a knife slides in easily.
Split open, top with cottage cheese, corn, beans and herbs — build a "toppings bar" and let each of you load your own.

minestrone_style_bean_pasta_soup.name: Minestrone-Style Bean & Pasta Soup
minestrone_style_bean_pasta_soup.note: Very light, very cheap — good on a day you want something easy on the stomach. Keeps 4 days (pasta softens further, still fine).
steps: Sauté onion, carrot, celery in oil, 6 min.
Add stock, tomatoes, cabbage and beans, simmer 15 min.
Add pasta, cook a further 8–10 min until tender. Season.

miso_soup_with_tofu_vegetables.name: Miso Soup with Tofu & Vegetables
miso_soup_with_tofu_vegetables.note: A starter or side, not a full meal on its own — pair with the sushi rolls or the teriyaki tofu bowl.
steps: Heat water until just below boiling — don't let it boil once the miso goes in.
Whisk in miso paste until dissolved.
Add tofu and spinach, warm through 3–4 min. Top with spring onion.

ingredients.prep: grated or diced, or a handful of berries

overnight_oats_no_cook.name: Overnight Oats (No-Cook)
overnight_oats_no_cook.note: The best option for a rushed morning — make two nights' worth at once and it's ready before you're properly awake. Keeps 2–3 days in the fridge if you want to prep further ahead.
steps: Stir oats, yogurt, milk and honey together in two jars or bowls.
Add the fruit — stir it through, or layer it on top.
Cover and refrigerate overnight (at least 4 hours). Eat cold, straight from the fridge.

pan_fried_gnocchi_with_onion_herbs.name: Pan-Fried Gnocchi with Onion & Herbs
pan_fried_gnocchi_with_onion_herbs.note: This is the classic boil-then-fry method — the pan-frying is what makes gnocchi worth cooking over plain pasta. Best fresh and crisp; if reheating, use a hot dry pan rather than the microwave so they don't turn mushy.
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil. Cook gnocchi per packet instructions (usually 2–3 min — they float when done), in 2–3 batches so the pot doesn't get crowded. Drain well, toss with a little oil so they don't stick together.
Meanwhile, sauté the onion in butter over medium heat, 8–10 min, until soft and starting to turn golden.
Add the drained gnocchi to the pan with the herbs, and fry 6–8 min, stirring only occasionally, until they pick up some golden-brown spots.
Season, stir through parsley, scatter cheese over if using.

pasta_with_creamy_mushroom_sauce.name: Pasta with Creamy Mushroom Sauce
pasta_with_creamy_mushroom_sauce.note: A basic white sauce (béchamel) with mushrooms folded in — the same sauce works spooned over Loaded Baked Potatoes instead of the toppings bar, for a richer version. Best fresh; reheats gently on the stove with a splash of milk to loosen it.
steps: Boil pasta per packet instructions.
Meanwhile, sauté onion and garlic in butter, 3 min. Add mushrooms, cook 7–8 min until they release their liquid and it mostly evaporates.
Sprinkle flour over, stir 1 min to coat. Gradually whisk in milk, a splash at a time, until smooth.
Simmer 6–8 min, stirring often, until it coats the back of a spoon. Season with salt, pepper and a little nutmeg. Toss with the drained pasta.

pasta_with_lentil_bolognese.name: Pasta with Lentil "Bolognese"
pasta_with_lentil_bolognese.note: Lower in fat than the jarred-sauce version, and cheaper. Keeps 4 days, freezes well.
steps: Sauté onion, carrot, garlic in oil, 6 min.

Add tomatoes and lentils (plus 300ml water if using dried lentils), simmer 25–30 min until the lentils are fully soft and the sauce has thickened — brown/green lentils take longer than red, so don't rush this.
Boil pasta, combine.

pasta_with_store_sauce_cheese.name: Pasta with Store Sauce & Cheese
pasta_with_store_sauce_cheese.note: Go easy on the cheese portion — it's most of the fat in this dish. Best fresh; reheats fine for 2–3 days.
steps: Boil pasta per packet instructions.
Warm the sauce, stir in spinach or zucchini if using.
Combine, top with grated cheese.

pea_lemon_risotto.name: Pea & Lemon Risotto
pea_lemon_risotto.note: The only real technique in this whole plan is "add stock gradually and stir" — no special equipment needed. A lighter Italian main; pair with a simple salad if you want more food on the plate. Best fresh, doesn't reheat as well as the others.
steps: Sauté onion and garlic in oil, 5 min. Add rice, stir 1–2 min to coat in the oil.
Add warm stock a ladle at a time, stirring often, waiting for each to be absorbed before adding the next — about 18–20 min total.
Stir in peas for the last 5 min. Off the heat, stir in lemon zest, juice and cheese. Season.

ingredients.prep: chopped, with spinach & bell pepper or whatever's in the fridge

quick_veggie_omelette.name: Quick Veggie Omelette
quick_veggie_omelette.note: Do these one at a time rather than doubling in one pan — the first stays warm while the second cooks, and it's easier to fold neatly.
steps: Whisk eggs with a splash of milk, salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat, add the vegetables, sauté 2–3 min until just softened.
Pour in the eggs, tilt the pan to spread evenly. Cook 2–3 min until mostly set, fold in half, cook a further minute.

ramen_with_egg.name: Ramen with Egg
ramen_with_egg.note: Your existing fallback — good for the flexible day when neither of you wants to cook properly.
steps: Cook noodles per packet, adding vegetables in the last 2 min.

Cook the eggs separately: for soft-boiled, lower eggs into simmering water 6–7 min then transfer to cold water and peel; for poached, crack into barely-simmering water 3 min. Top each bowl with one egg just before serving.

ingredients.prep: olive oil + lemon juice to dress; Garden Salad
thin red onion; White Bean & Vegetable Salad
olive oil + vinegar to dress; White Bean & Vegetable Salad

simple_salads_two_ways.name: Simple Salads, Two Ways
simple_salads_two_ways.note: The bean version has real protein in it, unlike the garden salad — better as a stand-alone light meal rather than a side.
steps: Garden Salad: toss the lettuce, tomato, cucumber and red onion together, scatter the crumbled cheese over the top, then dress with olive oil and a squeeze of lemon juice just before serving.
White Bean & Vegetable Salad: combine the drained white beans, cherry tomatoes, cucumber and red onion, stir through the chopped parsley, then dress with olive oil and vinegar and season to taste.

simple_sandwiches_two_ways.name: Simple Sandwiches, Two Ways
simple_sandwiches_two_ways.note: No cooking required for the second one. Both are here mainly for variety on nights you want something in five minutes rather than a proper batch dish.
steps: Grilled Cheese & Tomato: butter one side of each bread slice, layer cheese and tomato slices between the unbuttered sides, then grill in a pan over medium heat, 2–3 min per side, until golden and the cheese has melted.
Hummus, Cucumber & Roasted Pepper: spread hummus on the bread or wrap, layer in the cucumber, roasted pepper and spinach, then fold or close and slice in half — no cooking needed for this one.

simple_veggie_burgers.name: Simple Veggie Burgers
simple_veggie_burgers.note: Your own dish — recipe here mainly for the shopping list and quantities. Patties keep 3 days; assemble the burger fresh each time.
steps: Mash beans well, mix in breadcrumbs, egg, onion and spices until it holds together — add more breadcrumbs if too wet.
Shape into 6 patties. Chill 10 min if you have time (helps them hold together).
Pan-fry in a little oil, 4–5 min per side until firm and browned.
Serve in buns with lettuce, tomato and whatever condiments you like.

soft_tacos_with_beans_salsa.name: Soft Tacos with Beans & Salsa
soft_tacos_with_beans_salsa.note: The lightest dish in this section by far — beans and vegetables carry it rather than cheese or oil. Filling stores well 4 days; assemble fresh each time.
steps: Sauté onion and garlic, add beans, spices and a splash of water, mash lightly with a fork, simmer 10 min.
Warm the tortillas briefly in a dry pan.
Fill with the bean mixture, cabbage, salsa, a squeeze of lime and parsley.

stewed_potatoes_beans_peppers.name: Stewed Potatoes with Bell Pepper & Beans
stewed_potatoes_beans_peppers.note: Scaled up to a full 6-portion batch dish — sauté the aromatics well before adding the potatoes, that's where most of the flavor comes from.
steps: Sauté diced onion, carrot and bell pepper in the oil until softened.
Add cubed potatoes and tomato paste mixed with a splash of water, cover and simmer until the potatoes are tender.
Stir in the drained beans and cook a few minutes more.
Finish with pressed garlic and black pepper, adjusting salt to taste.

ingredients.prep: or water, or half and half
sliced, or a handful of berries
or brown sugar; pinch of cinnamon (optional)

stovetop_oatmeal_your_way.name: Stovetop Oatmeal, Your Way
stovetop_oatmeal_your_way.note: Water gives a lighter bowl, milk a creamier and more filling one. Swap the banana for whatever fruit is around — grated apple and cinnamon, or a spoon of jam, both work well.
steps: Combine oats, milk or water and a pinch of salt in a small pot.
Bring to a gentle simmer, stirring occasionally, 5–6 min, until thick and creamy — add a splash more liquid if it gets too thick.
Spoon into bowls, top with sliced fruit, a drizzle of honey and cinnamon.

teriyaki_tofu_rice_bowl.name: Teriyaki Tofu Rice Bowl
teriyaki_tofu_rice_bowl.note: The most "full dinner"-sized dish in this section. Keeps 3 days — tofu softens slightly on reheating.
steps: Pan-fry tofu cubes in oil until golden, set aside.
Mix soy sauce, honey, vinegar, minced garlic, grated ginger and the cornstarch with a splash of water.
Pour over the tofu in the pan, simmer 2–3 min until glossy and thickened by the cornstarch.
Serve over rice with steamed broccoli.

ingredients.prep: mixed veg: broccoli, carrot, bell pepper

tofu_vegetable_stir_fry_with_rice.name: Tofu & Vegetable Stir-Fry with Rice
tofu_vegetable_stir_fry_with_rice.note: Your best protein option in this list. Keeps 3 days — tofu softens a little on reheating but stays good.
steps: Pat tofu dry, pan-fry cubes in a little oil until golden on a few sides, 6–8 min. Set aside.
In the same pan, stir-fry vegetables and garlic 6–8 min.
Return tofu, add soy sauce (mixed with cornstarch + splash of water if using), toss 1–2 min.
Serve over rice.

vegetable_dumplings_potstickers.name: Vegetable Dumplings (Potstickers)
vegetable_dumplings_potstickers.note: Store-bought wrappers make this far easier than it sounds. A lighter dish — pair with rice or a simple stir-fried veg side for a full meal. Best fresh.
steps: Finely chop the cabbage, carrot and mushroom, salt lightly and let sit 10 min, then squeeze out as much liquid as you can — this stops the filling going watery and tearing the wrappers.
Mix the drained vegetables with garlic, ginger and soy sauce for the filling.
Place a spoonful in each wrapper, fold and seal the edges with a dab of water.
Pan-fry in oil 2–3 min until golden on the bottom, add a splash of water, cover and steam 5 min.

vegetable_egg_frittata.name: Vegetable & Egg Frittata
vegetable_egg_frittata.note: On the lighter side — good with a slice of bread or a simple tomato salad alongside. Keeps 3 days, good cold too.
steps: Parboil the diced potato in salted water about 8 min until just tender but not falling apart, then drain well.
Preheat oven to 190°C. Sauté onion in an oven-safe pan, 5 min, then layer in the parboiled potato and spinach.
Whisk eggs with milk, salt and pepper, pour over the vegetables, scatter cheese on top.
Cook on the stovetop 3–4 min until the edges set, then finish in the oven 15–18 min until just firm in the middle.

vegetable_spring_rolls.name: Vegetable Spring Rolls
vegetable_spring_rolls.note: Your own dish — this is the fresh, no-cook version. Light on its own, so good paired with the fried rice or a bowl of miso soup for a fuller meal. Best eaten same-day.
steps: Soak the rice vermicelli in just-boiled water 5–8 min until soft, then drain and rinse in cold water so it doesn't clump.
Dip a rice paper sheet in warm water a few seconds until pliable.
Lay flat, fill with shredded veg and the drained noodles, fold in the sides and roll tightly.
Serve with a soy-vinegar dipping sauce. No frying needed for this version.

vegetable_sushi_rolls.name: Vegetable Sushi Rolls
vegetable_sushi_rolls.note: Your own dish — takes a couple of tries to roll neatly, but tastes fine even when it looks rough. Light on its own; pair with miso soup or the teriyaki tofu bowl for a fuller meal. Don't overfill: a thin rice layer and thin veg strips roll and seal much more easily than a thick one, and a torn sheet is easy to patch with a second sheet — that's what the extra 2 sheets are for.
steps: Cook rice, then stir through the vinegar-sugar-salt mix while still warm. Let cool to room temperature.
Lay nori on a clean towel or mat, spread a thin, even layer of rice, leaving a gap at the top edge.
Lay a modest amount of vegetable strips near the bottom edge — overfilling is the #1 cause of tearing — then roll tightly using the towel or mat to guide it, wetting the top edge to seal.
Slice with a wet, sharp knife into pieces.

ingredients.prep: cut into strips, toasted, to top

vegetarian_tortilla_soup.name: Vegetarian Tortilla Soup
vegetarian_tortilla_soup.note: A light one — good on its own for lunch, or pair with a quesadilla wedge if you want a bigger dinner.
steps: Sauté onion and garlic, add spices, then tomatoes, stock, beans and corn.
Simmer 20 min. Season with lime juice.
Top with toasted tortilla strips just before serving.

yogurt_granola_parfait.name: Yogurt & Granola Parfait
yogurt_granola_parfait.note: Genuinely just assembly. Use plain yogurt over flavored to keep the sugar down — the honey adds enough sweetness on its own.
steps: Layer yogurt, granola and fruit in glasses or bowls.
Drizzle with honey.
